title: Critical telemetry gap and degradation action workshop
topics: Telemetry gaps around KV cache misses
degradation pattern during nightly batch spikes
summary: Workshop to review a recent production degradation tied to missing telemetry for prefix cache evictions. Goal: align on root cause hypotheses, immediate mitigations, and a 2-week verification plan including benchmarks and compliance artifacts.
action_items: Marco Ruiz - run KV cache integrity sweep, export eviction traces, and upload to shared s3://evg-redwood/telemetry - due 2026-06-26
Priya Nair - prepare a targeted diagnostic build with additional eviction logging and less aggressive batching for canary - due 2026-06-25
Alex Chen - share Redwood incident diagnostic playbook, SOC2/auditing excerpt, and the recommended fallback config - due 2026-06-24
Jin Park - correlate Evergreen's batch job schedule with Redwood request timestamps and share a pivot table - due 2026-06-27
Samir Patel - schedule a 30-min follow-up canary review call for 2026-06-29 14:00 UTC and invite product/security - due 2026-06-24
next_steps: Redwood to deliver diagnostic build and short doc describing logging flags
Customer to run 24h canary with reduced batching and send traces
Joint bench: run synthetic workload that reproduces nightly spike and measure latency/cost delta
Agree on formal RCA template and compliance checklist for regulators
notes: Customer emphasized need for an auditable chain for retention; Anita asked about HSM/KMS logs and retention windows
There was confusion early in the call about which cluster the error originated from (us-east-1a vs us-east-2a) - logs clarified it was a single host group
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: alright everyone thanks for joining, uh we know this is a follow up to last night's degradation, we're going to run through what we saw and, um, work through actions.
[00:00:12] Laura Kim: thanks Alex, appreciate it. quick note, execs are asking for timeline and what we need to do to avoid recurrence.
[00:00:20] Priya Nair: hi, i'm Priya, i'll be the SE on this. quick TLDR: we observed a step-in latency increase around 02:00 UTC correlating with your overnight batch job. initial telemetry had gaps - specifically eviction events for the prefix KV cache weren't captured.
[00:00:38] Marco Ruiz: yes and to add, our team's alert saw high p95 and then we had downstream retries, it magnified. i don't think the model itself regressed.
[00:00:46] Derek O'Neal: just to be clear, the batch job is a heavy write/refresh to embeddings store every night - could that cause cache churn?
[00:00:55] Priya Nair: absolutely, batches that rewrite embedding indices will evict prefixes; if eviction logs aren't flowing, Redwood's autoscaler and fallback policies can't respond properly, so you get larger batch sizes in-flight and longer latencies.
[00:01:12] Jin Park: we saw a bunch of 5xx timeouts in the app logs but the request ids didn't line up with Redwood trace ids. there's a mapping issue somewhere.
[00:01:20] Alex Chen: that's the telemetry gap — some trace sampling or agent restart around 01:55 stripped the eviction events. i've seen similar when kube node restarts cause short-lived agent disconnects.
[00:01:33] Anita Bose: from compliance, we need guaranteed retention of audit logs for 90 days, and we need proof that missing telemetry didn't hide data access. what's Redwood's angle?
[00:01:44] Samir Patel: we log keystore and access events to the audit log. even if eviction events were missing, the access records for the requests are still present. we'll pull those and map them to your ids.
[00:01:56] Marco Ruiz: ok, so main hypothesis is: node restart -> telemetry agent restart -> eviction events dropped -> autoscaler didn't observe cache churn -> batching grew -> latency spike. any other candidates?
[00:02:08] Priya Nair: another possibility is a misconfiguration of the agent's forwarder where the sampling window was set to 1/10 under load; that can look like a node flapping issue but is config.
[00:02:20] Laura Kim: do we also have a fallback configuration? last night we saw some 429s then a cascade of retries.
[00:02:27] Priya Nair: yes, by default Redwood has tiered fallback: first try smaller model variant, then rate-limit, then queue. but those require telemetry signals to trigger correctly. with missing signals the system stayed on larger model/host pool.
[00:02:40] Marco Ruiz: that explains the cost surge too. CTO is asking for proof we can hit cost/latency SLOs consistently for audit.
[00:02:49] Alex Chen: action plan in short: collect missing traces, run a canary with reduced batching and increased eviction logging, and prepare an auditable artifact.
[00:02:56] Jin Park: what's the easiest way to get those traces from Redwood? we need them mapped to our request ids.
[00:03:04] Priya Nair: we'll provide a diagnostic build with enhanced eviction logging and an id-mapping helper script; you run it in canary and upload artifacts to the shared s3.
[00:03:12] Derek O'Neal: will that add latency? we can't have canary adding noisy latency to production.
[00:03:18] Priya Nair: negligible for short runs; logging is async and we throttle write frequency. it's safe for a controlled 24h window.
[00:03:25] Anita Bose: about retention and encryption — are those logs under customer KMS or Redwood's? we need separation for compliance.
[00:03:34] Samir Patel: for Private and Dedicated customers we support customer-managed KMS. for hosted we can configure envelope encryption with customer keys depending on plan; i'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[00:03:45] Laura Kim: can you confirm whether any PII touched the logs last night?
[00:03:49] Alex Chen: short answer: no customer payloads were stored in eviction logs; they contain metadata — keys and sizes — but we'll scrub anything that looks like identifiers before sharing.
[00:03:58] Marco Ruiz: dataset: we also saw a correlation with autoscaler events - nodes were being spun up but not fast enough. is there a quick autoscaler tweak?
[00:04:08] Priya Nair: yes, you can reduce the batch window and set a lower scale-up cool-down so the pool reacts faster to cache-churn. we'll recommend concrete numbers in the doc.
[00:04:16] Alex Chen: question for Redwood team: is there a recommended rate-limit policy to prevent cascade retries?
[00:04:21] Priya Nair: adaptive rate limiting is best: start with per-token rate caps and backoff on 5xx. we can share our preset that many customers use during heavy batch windows.
[00:04:31] Jin Park: re: mapping issue, we'll provide a pivot of app->redwood ids, but if there are gaps, how do we proceed?
[00:04:38] Samir Patel: if mapping gaps exist we'll use timing buckets + host hashes to correlate; not perfect but good enough for RCA.
[00:04:46] Laura Kim: okay we need this all in writing — can you send the diagnostic plan and proposed config changes?
[00:04:51] Alex Chen: yes, i will. samir will add KMS/retention notes. priya will ship the build.
[00:04:57] Marco Ruiz: about timelines — can we run the canary Friday night? our batch is nightly at 01:30 UTC, we'd prefer Friday to avoid business traffic.
[00:05:06] Priya Nair: friday night works, we'll coordinate. plan: run 24h starting 20:00 UTC Friday.
[00:05:12] Derek O'Neal: one more ask — can we have a readout template for the audit team so they can sign off after the canary?
[00:05:18] Anita Bose: yes that's crucial.
[00:05:20] Samir Patel: we'll provide a compliance readout template with the artifacts checklist.
[00:05:25] Alex Chen: ok moving into some deeper technical questions — what exact eviction metric was missing?
[00:05:30] Priya Nair: the eviction_delta counter and per-prefix kv_hit_ratio. those two are how the autoscaler decides to shift batching thresholds.
[00:05:41] Marco Ruiz: and the agent that forwards those metrics, can it drop them if memory pressure spikes?
[00:05:46] Priya Nair: in low-memory conditions the forwarder can employ sampling; we usually set a pressure threshold. part of the diagnostic is to inspect agent logs for OOM or backpressure.
[00:05:57] Jin Park: we'll check node-level dmesg and kube events and upload them.
[00:06:02] Alex Chen: good. one wrinkle: you mentioned two clusters, but logs show it was the eu-west cluster, not us-east; please verify in your side as well.
[00:06:12] Laura Kim: noted, we'll confirm.
[00:06:15] Priya Nair: any other compliance flags?
[00:06:18] Anita Bose: just ensure the chain of custody for logs — where they live, who has access, rotation policy. and redact anything that could be considered user-identifiable in the export.
[00:06:29] Alex Chen: understood. we'll scrub and provide checksums.
[00:06:33] Marco Ruiz: sample size for the bench — what do you recommend to reproduce the spike?
[00:06:38] Priya Nair: mirror your nightly batch load and increase concurrency by 20% for spike reproduction; run 3 trials and we should see the same pattern if the hypothesis is correct. we'll provide the script.
[00:06:47] Derek O'Neal: how about rollback plan if canary shows new instability?
[00:06:51] Priya Nair: rollback is simple — revert agent flags and scale settings, and promote previous autoscaler config. we'll include steps in the runbook.
[00:07:00] Alex Chen: ok time check — we've captured actions. i'll recap and then open for any last comments.
[00:07:05] Alex Chen: recap: Redwood delivers diagnostic build + logging doc, Evergreen runs 24h canary with reduced batching, both sides upload artifacts, then joint bench and readout with compliance template. follow up canary review 2026-06-29 14:00 UTC.
[00:07:20] Laura Kim: thanks all. appreciate the thoroughness.
[00:07:23] Marco Ruiz: thanks, see you on the 29th.
[00:07:26] Anita Bose: bye.
[00:07:28] [call ends]
